question: What is the state of research on in-context learning (ICL): its definition, training, prompt design, analysis, applications and open challenges?
contributions: Formal definition of ICL and its relation to prompt learning and few-shot learning
Taxonomy (Fig 2) of training strategies, prompt designing strategies and analysis
Review of applications (data engineering, model augmentation, knowledge updating) and modalities beyond text
Small own comparison of demonstration selection methods (Table 2) and scoring functions (Tables 4-5)
Challenges: efficiency and scalability, generalization, long-context ICL

limits: Survey authors concede possible omissions of valuable work in demonstration design and ICL analysis (Limitations).
Many surveyed papers did not use the most up-to-date models (Limitations).
Analytical/theory studies mostly cover simple tasks and small models (Sec 5.2).

Own experiments are small: 8 demonstrations, 4 models up to 8B, 5 classification datasets, 1000 test items; no agent, planning or tool-use ICL is covered (planning appears only via the Valmeekam benchmark mention).
Efficiency/scalability fixes (distilling demonstrations) need parameter access, impractical for closed models (Sec 7).
Table 5 caption (10k test set) conflicts with Appendix B (1000 test items for some datasets).
practices: Add a warmup (instruction-tuning) stage before ICL inference even though it is optional (App A.1).
Choose demonstrations nearest to the query by embedding similarity (kNN, KATE) as a baseline; supervised retrievers (EPR) improve on heuristic ones (Sec 4.1.1).
Treat demonstration selection method as model-dependent; test on the target model (Table 2).
Order demonstrations with the closest example last or simple-to-complex; order sensitivity is universal (Sec 4.1.3).
Use chain-of-thought demonstrations for complex reasoning, and LLM-generated instructions/demonstrations to reduce template-writing effort (Sec 4.2, App A.2).
Use Direct scoring for efficiency, PPL for stability and coverage, Channel for imbalanced data (Sec 4.3, Tables 3-5).
Do not assume more demonstrations are better in long-context settings (Sec 7).

terms.definition: a paradigm that allows language models to learn tasks given only a few examples in the form of demonstration.
categorized by whether k and the demonstration examples belong to the same task; in cross-task, different examples have their own instructions.
prompts can be discrete templates or soft parameters; ICL can be regarded as a subclass of prompt tuning where demonstration examples are part of the prompt.
adapting model parameters to perform a task with a limited number of supervised examples; ICL needs no parameter updates.
a continual training stage between pretraining and ICL inference that modifies or adds parameters.
substitutes natural language labels with arbitrary symbols to force learning input-label mappings from context.
Direct: P(y|C,x); PPL: perplexity of the whole sequence with candidate label; Channel: conditional probability of the input given the label.
attention heads that replicate previous patterns for next-token prediction, progressively developing ICL capabilities.
